[Package]
Name="tsa_lib_omni_bus"
Version="2.0.1.6"
Release=""
ID=629de5535a08fe90e18097d9657ec998
File Format="vip"
Format Version="2017"
Display Name="Omni-Bus"


[Description]
Description="The Omni-Bus Maps Tags to Most LabVIEW datatypes.\0A\0AThe difference between this and other Tagbus API's, the "Bus"  API that plugs in to the Omni-Bus class factory to make Tag to Value mappings from multiple different buses.\0AThe buses extend the TSI Abstract Data Classes and so the data can be accessed as the abstract class or as the specific variable. There is API to access both methods\0A\0ABuses included are: \0A- 'Local Bus', this is a DVR based local variable. But future buses include shared variables, cRIO scan engine IO, \0A- 'Aggregator Bus' this adds descrete classes to the API, such as constant classes.\0A- 'Remap Bus' this is a wrapper bus is used to rename the exisiting tags\0A- 'Fault Injection Bus', This is a wrapper bus that wraps the other bus value objects with the Fault Injection objects.\0A\0AExamples are available"
Summary="This is a Tag to Variable API"
License="GPL-3.0"
Copyright="Copyright (c) 2024, TSA"
Distribution=""
Vendor="TSA"
URL="https://github.com/timstreeter/Omni-Bus"
Packager="Tim"
Demo="FALSE"
Release Notes="V2.0.1.6\0AThe previous changes broke Remap bus. This is now fixed\0A\0AAdded Example 9 that highlights the usage of the "Multi" value access objects that makes it easier to access multiple values of the same type.\0A\0Av2.0.0.5\0AAdded the "Fault Injection Bus.lvclass"  decorator class. When added after other "Bus Access" Classes it can their value objects with the Fault Injection Value objects that add additional Fault Insertion Functionality. \0A\0AAn Example 8 is added to demo the Fault Injection features.\0A\0AOther changes are:\0A- LabVIEW polymorphic VI's don't work with dynamic dispatch methods so a wrapper "Static Get" VI's was needed. With changes I have made to how I implemented Fault Injection, the requirement for dynamic dispatch the omni-bus methods was not required so I was able to remove the redundant wrapper VI's. The downside is the polymorphic Get VI now point to different Get VI's and they will need to each reselected.\0A"
